Sri. T.Muniswamappa sold property bearing Municipal No. 146/2 South portion, Site No.8 situated at 7 th cross Malleshwaram, 7th Division of Bengaluru City in favour of plaintiff under the registered sale deed dated 18.03.1981 vide Document No.4853/1980-81, Volume No. 2846, Book No.1 at Page No. 75 to 77 in the office of Sub Registrar of Bengaluru.
After executing the sale deed, plaintiff was put in possession and enjoyment of the said property and since then, he is in the possession and enjoyment of the said property for more than 36 years.

After many years, he decided to construct house building in the said property and approached BBMP to mark sketch and BBMP officials identified the same and Assistant Executive Engineer, Gandhinagar Sub-Division, issued sketch to the suit property.
The plaintiff approached concerned department for building sanction plan to make the construction on the suit property.
The Assistant Executive Engineer sanctioned the plan for construction of building in the suit property and plaintiff started construction of building in the suit property.
On 23.12.2017, the plaintiff started O.S.No.262/2018 construction work in the suit property.
But on the next day, defendants started quarreling with plaintiff not to put up any construction over the suit schedule property without giving any reason.

When plaintiff was not in the place of suit property, the defendants used to threaten the labourers of the construction of building and they are interfering with the suit property with the help of their agents and goondas,
which has been successfully resisted by plaintiff.

The defendants are not having any kind of right,
title or interest over the suit property.

But inspite of resistance by the plaintiff, they are trying to disturb the peaceful possession of the suit property and they and their family members are making all hectic efforts with the help of anti elements to encroach the suit property.

The plaintiff approached Sheshadripuram police station on 24.12.2017 who have refused to register the case stating that, dispute is civil in nature and same is required to be addressed by the Civil Court.
Hence plaintiff is constrained to file this suit against the defendants seeking the relief of permanent injunction.
The defendant No.1 to 4 filed their written statement and denied the contents of plaint.
They have contended that, the plaintiff has approached this court with malafide intention and suit is not maintainable either in law or in facts and liable to be dismissed.

It is further contended that, the police authorities summoned the defendants with regard to the complaint of plaintiff and defendants appeared before them and given their statement stating that, they have nothing to do with the suit property and plaintiff on the strength of documents created by him is trying to claim a portion of ancestral property of the defendants as suit schedule property and for illegal acts of the plaintiff, they have resisted.
The plaintiff is at liberty to construct in the suit in his property.
But no law will permit the plaintiff to construct a building on some other's property claiming as his property.

He has approached this court on wrong presumption and sought the relief of permanent injunction against the defendants to their ancestral property which is highly illegal.

Till the year 2015, plaintiff kept quiet or might be searching for his property and for the first time on 14.12.2015, he approached the jurisdictional police with false complaint alleging that defendants have dumped sheet and police authorities issued notice, for which defendants have explained the issue and submitted the documents pertaining to their ancestral property.

sentences.text: Unless the defendant proves better title, plaintiff with title must be held to be in possession.

The plaintiff's possession is not only de facto but also dejure.

So far as counter claim is concerned, it is submitted in the written argument in paragraph No.13 that the counter claim property is a different property and there is no overlap between the two properties and counter claim is not maintainable.
It is settled law that, counter claim must relate to the same cause of action or same property.
But it concerns a different property altogether.
It is also settled principles of law that, property is vacant and both parties claim possession.
The possession follows ownership and title holder deemed in possession.
The defendant must rebut the presumption by producing strong title or possession thereof.
Mere adjacency or claim based on neighboring property O.S.No.262/2018 cannot dislodge the owner of Sy.No. 29.
The plaintiff's lawful possession over the vacant schedule site is established by operation of law and documents entitling him to protection under Sections 38 and 41 of Specific Relief Act.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the property is vacant and unoccupied, the test of physical possession becomes secondary.
It is settled law that, counter claim must relate to the same cause of action or same property.
But it concerns a different property altogether.
It is also settled principles of law that, property is vacant and both parties claim possession.
The possession follows ownership and title holder deemed in possession.
The defendant must rebut the presumption by producing strong title or possession thereof.
Mere adjacency or claim based on neighboring property O.S.No.262/2018 cannot dislodge the owner of Sy.No. 29.
The plaintiff's lawful possession over the vacant schedule site is established by operation of law and documents entitling him to protection under Sections 38 and 41 of Specific Relief Act.
The defendants have failed to prove the title by any registered document for Sy.No. 29 or suit schedule property.
Hence defendants' actual legal holding should be only 1140 square feet, not 5040 square feet, clearly proving the boundary manipulation and encroachment into the plaintiff's Municipal No. 146/2.
Defendants with their local influence have extended their boundary towards north into Survey No.
29 under the cover of fabricated survey map.
It is trite of law that final decree cannot enlarge or alter the extent and boundaries fixed under the preliminary decree.
